reuse.name: fixFileModesJob (existing repair scaffold)

why_tier: Requires reasoning about a data-integrity divergence (stale book_file.FilePath rows vs. the real on-disk path a write-back resolved to) before any fix can be scoped — exactly the kind of ambiguous root-cause judgment call that needs a strong model, and it sits on the organize/file-path prod-data path (review_critical).
goal: Before writing any code: determine WHY a sampled book's /files API row points at a path that does not exist on disk while the write-back demonstrably wrote to a different, real path for the same book (organize moved the file without updating book_file.FilePath? a duplicate book_file row exists, one stale and one live?). Only once that is known can the correct fix be scoped: either (a) extend fix-file-modes with a disk-walk mode that finds 0600 files under the organizer root independent of book_file rows, or (b) hand-repair the specific 124 residual files via the documented `find ... -exec chmod` one-liner without touching the underlying row bug, or (c) fix the row-update path in organize/write-back so book_file.FilePath never goes stale after a move.
background: fix-file-modes (internal/maintenance/jobs/fix_file_modes.go) is scoped deliberately tight: only files enumerated via store.GetAllBookFilesCore(), owned by the service uid, and currently mode 0600 (lines 24-29, 46-67).
1,547 files were already repaired by this job in production; 124 remain 0600 after that run, per the TODO item's field observation.

The item's own investigation found the residue files have mtimes in the canary write-back window, meaning the write-back process DID touch them — but the enumeration (which reads book_file.FilePath rows) does not see them, implying either the row's path is stale or a duplicate row exists.

The item's concrete example: a book's /files API row points at '.../The Seven Deadly Demons 3 - Dungeon of Pride/Dungeon of Pride.m4b' (ENOENT) while the real file is at '.../The Seven Deadly Demons/Dungeon of Pride/...' — i.e. the book's series-numbered folder name in the row does not match the real (unnumbered) folder on disk.
steps: DESIGN QUESTION (must be answered before implementation): for the sampled book (or a fresh small sample of the 124), is the stale book_file.FilePath row (a) a row organize failed to update after moving the file, (b) a duplicate/orphaned book_file row alongside a second, correct row for the same book, or (c) something else (e.g. a rename collision from generateTargetPath, see the sibling L2945 item)? Investigate via: querying book_file rows for one affected book (GetBookFilesByBookID or equivalent), comparing FilePath values against `find <organizer-root> -type f -user <service-user> -perm 600` results, and checking organizer move-tracking logs/activity entries around the write-back's mtime window for that book.

Once root cause is known, if it is (a) or (b): decide whether to patch the responsible organize/write-back code path (schema/data-integrity fix, needs its own scoped ticket) versus purely repairing symptoms.

In parallel/regardless: extend fix-file-modes (internal/maintenance/jobs/fix_file_modes.go) with an optional disk-walk mode — walk the configured organizer root(s) for regular files owned by the service uid with mode 0600, independent of book_file rows — gated behind a new DefaultParams() field (e.g. `DiskWalk bool`), defaulting false so the existing behavior is unchanged by default.
Never delete or move any file as part of this repair — REPOINT/repair only, per the project's standing rule.

If a manual one-off is chosen instead of/in addition to the code fix, it must go through docs/operations/pending-prod-actions.md as a prod_run, not be executed directly (see decision #14 in the owner list).

title: Decide how (or whether) dynamic collections stay fresh outside manual materialize
verdict_evidence: Confirmed at HEAD: collections have MaterializedBookIDs (internal/database/store.go, Collection struct) evaluated only at creation, on query edit, on native-API read, and via POST /api/v1/collections/:id/materialize (internal/server/handlers/collections.go:371 MaterializeCollection). No background refresh mechanism exists — unlike playlists, which already have a Dirty flag + push worker (internal/database/pebble_store_playlists.go:191,344,349,381; internal/database/pebble_quick_queries.go:92-128 MarkQuickQueryDirty/MarkAllQuickQueriesDirty pattern). The item poses an explicit either/or ('Either add one, or rename the concept') that no owner decision in this scope's list resolves.

verified_anchors.claim: Collection has a MaterializedBookIDs cache with no background refresh path
verified_anchors.expect: 1 hit, doc comment says 'Advisory only: readers that need live results re-evaluate'

verified_anchors.claim: the ABS read path serves MaterializedBookIDs directly, never live-evaluating
smart playlists already have a Dirty-flag pattern that collections lack
verified_anchors.expect: hits at L191, L344, L349, L381

reuse.name: playlist Dirty flag + push worker pattern
quick-query MarkQuickQueryDirty/MarkAllQuickQueriesDirty as a second precedent for dirty-marking on a cached derived view

why_tier: This is a product/architecture decision (build a background refresh mechanism vs. rename the feature to stop over-promising), not an implementation task — needs a decision-maker, not a coder.
goal: DECISION NEEDED, not code: should a query-backed ('dynamic') collection be kept fresh automatically — e.g. by giving Collection a Dirty flag set whenever a book that could match any dynamic collection's query changes, plus a background push worker analogous to the playlist one — or should the feature be renamed (e.g. 'saved search' / 'query collection, evaluated on write') so its actual behavior (creation-time snapshot, refreshed only on explicit action) matches its name? Either answer is a real, scoped follow-up ticket; this item alone should not be coded against without that decision.
background: A dynamic collection is evaluated at 4 specific moments only: creation, query edit, native-API GET (server side re-evaluates on read for the native path, per internal/server/handlers/collections.go:247-259's GetCollection), and POST .../materialize.

The ABS surface deliberately never live-evaluates (serves MaterializedBookIDs only), so a collection created via the native API and only ever viewed in an ABS client shows stale, creation-time membership indefinitely — this is the concrete user-facing symptom.
Smart playlists solved the equivalent problem already with a Dirty bool field plus a background push worker; that is the template IF the 'add a refresh mechanism' branch is chosen.
steps: 1. Surface this as an explicit decision question to the owner (or record it in the appropriate design-decisions doc) rather than picking an answer unilaterally.

2. If 'add a refresh mechanism' is chosen: model it directly on internal/database/pebble_store_playlists.go's Dirty flag pattern — add `Dirty bool` to database.Collection, mark it whenever any book potentially affecting a dynamic collection's query changes (this itself needs scoping: marking ALL dynamic collections dirty on every book write may be cheap enough given collection counts are typically small, unlike the whole-library playlist case — verify with a count query before assuming a naive 'mark all dirty' is too expensive), and add a background worker that re-materializes dirty dynamic collections periodically.

3. If 'rename the concept' is chosen: this is a much smaller change — update Collection.Type='dynamic' user-facing copy/docs to describe the actual, documented refresh triggers, and consider adding a 'last refreshed at' timestamp so users understand freshness without a background job.

4. Whichever path, add a regression test proving the ABS read path (h.collectionsPageBooks or wherever ABS resolves collection membership) reflects the chosen behavior explicitly, so this cannot regress silently again.
edge_cases: A dynamic collection whose query never matches anything (empty MaterializedBookIDs) should not be treated as 'broken' by whichever mechanism is chosen — it is a valid state.
If a background refresh worker is added, it must not become another whole-library O(n) loop without a bounded worker pool per this repo's CLAUDE.md concurrency mandate.
notes: Do not implement a refresh mechanism speculatively without the decision being made first — the 'rename' branch is a legitimate, much cheaper resolution and picking the expensive branch by default would be the wrong call if collections are lightly used.

title: Add a compare-and-swap on Collection.Version to PebbleStore.UpdateCollection
verdict_evidence: internal/database/pebble_store_collections.go:181-241 (UpdateCollection) unconditionally sets `col.Version = prev.Version + 1` (line 217) with no check that the caller's `col.Version` (the version it read before mutating) still matches `prev.Version` — confirming the item's claim of a read-modify-write race with no version check, even though Collection.Version already exists and is incremented on every write.

verified_anchors.claim: UpdateCollection increments Version unconditionally with no CAS check
all 6 call sites read-then-write, so col.Version is always populated with the just-read value before this call
Collection already carries a Version field

reuse.name: existing 'already in use' string-matched error pattern for translating a store error to an HTTP conflict

why_tier: A concurrency/CAS fix in the storage layer with parity needed across PebbleStore and MockStore, plus multiple call sites needing conflict-error translation — mechanical but touches enough files to warrant care.
goal: Add a compare-and-swap check to PebbleStore.UpdateCollection: reject the write with a distinguishable conflict error when the caller's col.Version does not match the currently-stored prev.Version, so two concurrent read-modify-write cycles (e.g. two AddBookToCollection calls) cannot silently lose one's change.
background: internal/server/handlers/abs/collections.go:288-330 (AddBookToCollection) and :332-371 (RemoveBookFromCollection) both read the collection via h.lookupCollection(c), mutate col.BookIDs in memory, then call h.collections.UpdateCollection(col) — classic read-modify-write with no protection.
internal/server/handlers/collections.go:280-345 (native PUT UpdateCollection) has the identical shape via h.load(c).

internal/database/pebble_store_collections.go:195-217 already loads `prev` via p.GetCollection(col.ID) inside UpdateCollection itself — the CAS check slots in right after that load, before the unconditional Version bump.
steps: 1. In internal/database/pebble_store_collections.go's UpdateCollection, immediately after `prev, err := p.GetCollection(col.ID)` and the nil-check (around line 195-201), add: `if col.Version != prev.Version { return fmt.Errorf("collection %s version conflict: expected %d, got %d", col.ID, prev.Version, col.Version) }`.

2. Update MockStore.UpdateCollection (internal/database/mock_store.go:1659) with the same CAS semantics for parity between the two Store implementations (dual-implementation divergence is exactly the class of bug #2406/#2410/#2411 fixed previously — do not let this be a third instance).

3. In internal/server/handlers/abs/collections.go's AddBookToCollection (line 324) and RemoveBookFromCollection (line 365), and in internal/server/handlers/collections.go's UpdateCollection (line 341), extend the existing `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "already in use")` conflict-detection pattern to also match `"version conflict"`, translating it to httputil.RespondWithConflict(c, ...) / respondError(c, http.StatusConflict, ...) instead of a 500.

4. Decide whether callers should retry-once (re-read, re-apply the same mutation, re-save) or simply surface the 409 to the client for a manual retry — given these are low-contention paths (single-book adds/removes), a bare 409 without auto-retry is the simpler, honest choice; do not add retry logic unless asked.
5. Bump version headers on all touched files.

title: Implement POST /api/session/local-all (batch local-session sync, accept both body shapes)

The design spec is unusually explicit here: docs/specs/2026-07-29-abs-sync-api-design.md:173 states '/api/session/local-all must return 200 and silently ignore unknown item IDs. goal: Add POST /api/session/local-all: accept a body that is EITHER a bare JSON array of local playback sessions OR an object shaped {"sessions": [...], "deviceInfo": {...}} (AudioBooth's shape), apply each session's progress via the existing resolveBookID + applyProgressUpdate pipeline (mirroring MediaProgressBatchUpdate's loop exactly), silently skip sessions naming an unknown item id, and always answer 200 — never a 4xx, per the spec's explicit warning that a 4xx here permanently wedges the client's offline replay queue.
background: A 'local session' in the ABS local-sync API represents an offline listening session a client recorded while disconnected and is now uploading; structurally it carries the same currentTime/duration/timeListened fields as the live /sync body (internal/server/handlers/abs/play.go's syncRequest, lines 335-340) plus an item identifier and (for AudioBooth) deviceInfo.

MediaProgressBatchUpdate (internal/server/handlers/abs/progress.go:157-184) already implements the identical shape for a DIFFERENT route (PATCH /api/me/progress/batch/update): bare array body, per-item resolveBookID + applyProgressUpdate, skip on unknown id, single final respondPlainOK — this is the template to copy, not invent from scratch.

The two required body shapes are genuinely different at the JSON level (array vs. object-wrapping-an-array), so the handler needs to peek at the raw body and branch, or unmarshal into a struct with a custom UnmarshalJSON that accepts both — a custom UnmarshalJSON on a wrapper type is the cleaner approach and avoids double-parsing.

title: Decide whether to wire real RecordChange/ChangeCounters or delete the dead change-summary log line that reads them
verdict_evidence: internal/logger/standard.go:62-63 confirms RecordChange and ChangeCounters are empty/nil stubs on StandardLogger (the type reporterLogger wraps via logger.New). internal/scanner/service.go:265-269 is the ONLY consumer of ChangeCounters in the whole codebase (`grep -rn '.ChangeCounters(' internal/` outside internal/logger returns exactly 1 hit), and it is dead: `counters != nil` is always false since StandardLogger.ChangeCounters() always returns nil, so the log line never fires. But even a fixed ChangeCounters would still report nothing today, because NOTHING calls RecordChange anywhere in the current scan/organize code paths (`grep -rln 'RecordChange(' internal/` outside internal/logger and the itunes adapter's pass-through definition returns zero real call sites) — so fixing ChangeCounters alone would not make the log line meaningful; RecordChange would ALSO need to be called from wherever books are actually created/updated during a scan. That is a real design question (where exactly should RecordChange be called, and is it worth it) that no owner decision in this scope covers.

why_tier: The fork (wire real change-tracking end-to-end vs. delete the always-false dead branch) requires judging whether book_create/book_update/book_skip counters are worth the effort of adding RecordChange call sites throughout the scanner, which is a scope decision, not a mechanical fix.
goal: DECISION NEEDED: is the scan-completion 'book changes: N created, M updated' log line (internal/scanner/service.go:265-269) worth making real — which requires BOTH fixing reporterLogger to carry a working RecordChange/ChangeCounters (e.g. by embedding logger.OperationLogger instead of a plain logger.New("operation") StandardLogger, or by giving reporterLogger its own change-counter state) AND adding actual RecordChange(...) calls at each book-create/update site in the scanner — or should the dead `counters != nil` branch simply be deleted as an honest no-op, since deleting it is far cheaper and nothing currently depends on the counters existing?
background: This is the sibling gap to the IsCanceled forwarding issue (TODO.md L4586, same scope) and the same UpdateProgress stub bug fixed 2026-08-16 (progress.go's own history comment) — all three (UpdateProgress, IsCanceled, RecordChange/ChangeCounters) trace back to the same BridgeQueue-elimination-era stub, but UpdateProgress alone has been fixed so far.

Unlike IsCanceled (which just needs forwarding to something that already works), RecordChange has NO live caller anywhere in the current scan/organize path — so 'just forward it' is not sufficient here; the deeper question is whether change-tracking counters were ever actually wired into the CURRENT scanner implementation at all, or whether this log line has been permanently empty since long before the 2026-05-11 BridgeQueue removal.

internal/logger/operation.go's OperationLogger already has a real, working RecordChange/ChangeCounters implementation (appends to a slice, increments a map) — proving the underlying mechanism is sound; the question is purely about wiring it into the currently-active scan/organize/reconcile logger path.
steps: 1. Determine historically whether the scanner ever called RecordChange in its book-create/update loop before the BridgeQueue removal (git log/blame on internal/scanner/service.go around the ChangeCounters() call site) — this tells you whether this is a REGRESSION to restore or a feature that was always aspirational/unwired.
2. Bring the wire-vs-delete decision to the owner with that history as context.

3. If wiring: (a) change LoggerFromReporter to embed a change-tracking-capable logger (either give reporterLogger its own change slice/counter map matching OperationLogger's approach, or literally embed *logger.OperationLogger instead of the plain StandardLogger from logger.New), (b) add RecordChange(logger.Change{...}) calls at the actual book-create and book-update sites in the scanner's per-file processing loop, using whatever Change struct shape OperationLogger.RecordChange already expects.

4. If deleting: remove the `counters := log.ChangeCounters()` / `if counters != nil && ...` block at internal/scanner/service.go:264-269 entirely, since it can never fire and is dead code, not a working feature with a bug.
notes: Do not fix ChangeCounters alone and declare this done — that would make the log line's `counters != nil` check pass while `counters["book_create"]` etc. are still always 0, which is a MORE misleading state than today's permanently-skipped line (a log claiming '0 created, 0 updated' during a scan that created 500 books reads as a false negative, worse than never printing at all).
